products.name: Memory over time
products.headline: Agent memory that knows when a fact stopped being true
products.pain: Your agent remembers that a customer moved, then answers with the old address. Most memory layers store facts; few can answer "what did we believe on 1 March" or cleanly retract a wrong fact.
for_whom: Teams shipping agents that talk to the same users for months (CRM, support, sales assistants)
Anyone evaluating Mem0, Zep/Graphiti or a homegrown store and needing an honest comparison on their own data
Regulated workflows where you must show what the agent knew at a given date
products.first_win: Your agent answers an "as of date D" question correctly on your own records, and a retracted fact stays retracted.

metrics.bench: Retracting a wrong fact (scenario 402), narrow test with a red control

limits: On LoCoMo temporal questions Mem0 beats us (76.5 vs 72.2, borderline significance); we publish it anyway.
The retraction result ties Mem0; it shows the scenario works, not that we are better.
The LoCoMo row and the retraction row are two different engines of ours, labelled as such.
DolphinBench numbers are source-session recall, not the full DolphinBench pass rate.
LongMemEval has not been run yet; it is next on the list.
extra_links: Open memory-bench leaderboard, rerun in CI

products.name: Second brain search
products.headline: Search your team's notes like it remembers everything
products.pain: Years of notes, calls and chats sit in Obsidian, Drive and Telegram. Keyword search misses meaning, vector search misses names and dates, and nobody measured which one your data needs.
for_whom: Operators, researchers and small teams with a large markdown or Obsidian vault
Teams who want their agents (Claude, Codex, Cursor) to read the same knowledge base over MCP
Anyone choosing between pgvector, Qdrant, LanceDB or SQLite and wanting numbers instead of opinions
products.first_win: On 20 real questions from your own notes, the right note lands in the top 5 more often, and the system says "not in your notes" instead of inventing an answer.

metrics.bench: memory-bench v0.1, 202 notes, 91 questions, rerun in CI
metrics.metric: Recall@5 / abstains when the answer is absent

limits: On the CI leaderboard a plain RAG reference still edges us on Recall@5 (0.93 vs 0.88); we win on refusing to answer when the note does not exist.
Plain BM25 beats every dense setup on name-heavy data; we tell you when you do not need vectors at all.
Our own reranker cost us 12 to 18 points of Recall@5; the benchmark caught it and we removed it.
Questions that point to one meeting by date are still the shared failure of every system we tested.

products.name: Synthetic cofounder
products.headline: An AI cofounder that keeps its character when you swap the model
products.pain: You built an agent persona that argues, says no and remembers your decisions. Then the vendor ships a new model and the persona quietly turns into a polite yes-man. Nobody measures that.
for_whom: Operators who want a sparring partner that pushes back with evidence, not a chat assistant
Teams running one agent persona across Claude, GPT, Gemini or Grok
Builders of companion or advisor products who need to prove character stability
products.first_win: Your persona scores within a measured band on two different models, on five tasks that probe character, not knowledge.

metrics.bench: Persona Portability Benchmark, 18 models, 5 tasks, blind 3-judge panel
First run, 7 models, same persona and frozen memory

limits: We found no public benchmark for one persona on many models, so we built one; it is ours and it is open.
The ruler moved by up to 0.8 between runs on unchanged models; we report it.
Stronger models fabricate more convincing evidence; the benchmark has a task for that.

products.name: Agent message bus
products.headline: Messages between agents on different machines, with a receipt for every task
products.pain: Machine A needs something from machine B, so a human copy-pastes between terminals. Or an agent hands off a task, nobody checks it landed, and silence gets read as success.
for_whom: Teams running Claude Code, Codex or Cursor agents on several machines
Engineers wiring A2A or MCP agents together who need delivery receipts, not hope
Anyone whose "human in the loop" has turned into "human as the courier"
products.first_win: Two of your machines exchange a task over two rails at once and the sender sees an explicit ACK, not silence.

metrics.bench: 103 days of fleet telemetry, task acknowledgements

limits: Less than half of tasks got a matched ACK; that gap is exactly what the protocol exposes and what we are fixing.
There is no mature public benchmark for inter-agent messaging; we publish raw telemetry and scripts instead.
Historical telemetry from our own fleet, not a test run on your machines.
extra_links: Coordination Decay: 103 days of a seven-machine fleet

products.name: Fleet consensus
products.headline: Let your machines agree on routine decisions and wake you only for risky ones
products.pain: Once agents run on several machines they drift apart, two of them commit conflicting changes, and every decision ends up back on your desk.
for_whom: Teams running Claude Code, Codex or Cursor agents on several machines
Engineers building inter-agent messaging (A2A, MCP) who want a protocol that has survived production
Anyone who needs machines to agree on routine decisions and wake a human only for risky ones
products.first_win: A routine change is proposed, accepted and independently verified by a second machine, and a risky one waits for you.

metrics.bench: 103 days of fleet telemetry, consensus log
rows: Risky (Tier-2) commits without prior human approval
Commits checked by an independent machine

limits: Proposals fell from 121 to 6 a month: a finding about coordination decay, published as such, not a success metric.
Historical telemetry from our own fleet; no public consensus benchmark exists.
Preprint on arXiv (cs.MA) is pending endorsement; the repository copy is canonical.
extra_links: Fleet deploy: roll a fix to every node and prove it landed

products.name: LLM spend audit
products.headline: Find out how much of your LLM bill is mechanics
products.pain: Your most expensive model runs shell commands and reads files all day, while cheaper subscriptions you already pay for sit idle. The vendor dashboard shows the total, not where it went.
for_whom: Teams paying for several LLM subscriptions and API keys at once
Engineering leads who need a per-task breakdown before cutting a contract
Anyone running agent harnesses (Claude Code, Codex) at volume
products.first_win: A one-page breakdown of your own transcripts: which share of tokens is judgement and which is mechanics that can move to a cheaper rail.

metrics.bench: Our hub, 7 days of output tokens on the top model

limits: Absolute totals are inflated by double counting in the transcripts; only the shares are reliable, and the tool says so.
Reads local transcripts only: no LLM call, no network, no API key.

products.name: MCP daemon diet
products.headline: Stop every agent session from spawning its own copy of every MCP server
products.pain: Each Claude or Codex session starts its own stdio copy of every MCP server. With 50 sessions open the machine swaps, the fans spin and nobody knows why.
for_whom: Anyone running many parallel agent sessions on one machine
Teams with Telegram, MongoDB, n8n or browser MCP servers in their config
Ops people who were told "just buy more RAM"
products.first_win: One shared MCP daemon per machine instead of one per session, and a measured RAM drop on your own machine.

metrics.bench: Our hub after the switch, same measuring script

limits: Summed RSS overstates real memory because pages are shared; the README says so.
Before removing a server we count real tool calls; servers that are used stay.

products.name: Second-opinion panel
products.headline: One reviewer model is one blind spot. Ask several families at once.
products.pain: You ask a model to review code and get confident findings. Half of them are about code it never saw. A single vendor also shares its own blind spots with the code it wrote.
for_whom: Teams letting agents write code and wanting an independent review before merge
Anyone with Claude, GPT, Gemini and Grok subscriptions who wants them to check each other
Leads who need an exit code that refuses to go green without a real second opinion
products.first_win: A review of one real pull request by three model families, with quorum counted by family and fake findings filtered out.

metrics.bench: Same repo, 4 models from 4 families, only the input changed

limits: One measured repository, four models; small sample, stated as such.
19 gotchas the panel found in its own code are listed in the repo.
